one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q3 2026 results should land around Nov 9-18, after Oct 31 (Q2 was Aug 10; Q3 2025 was Nov 10). EDGAR shows no new 6-K since the 9/29 H1 filing. Inside the window: the September production update, likely mid-October (the August one was filed Sep 16-17). Only the infrastructure section moved to quarterly, so the mining/AI metrics should still come out. Expect ~80-84 EH/s self-mining and AI ARR near $86-95M; an upside surprise would be A201 commitments being confirmed as executed or prepaid (>70% committed per the 9/29 release). Other movers: BTC (~$84.8k on 10/1) and hashprice, ATM sales under the $1B program (only $8.4M used by 9/29), and any Tydal financing or Rockdale lease headline. The stock fell from ~$12.3 to ~$10.5 over Sep 23-30. Short-term reversal and negative momentum roughly offset, so I keep a near-symmetric spread around spot (P(>=10.64)=0.495) at a monthly sigma of ~29%, close to 108%/3.5 = 31%. Unchanged in round 4: the site-coverage and discount-rate fixes move long-run value, not anything that resolves before Oct 31, and no event in the window bears on it.

fair_value.method: Blend of a site-by-site split-rate DCF (-$0.40; -$1.04 at a single 13.9% WACC), a site-by-site SOTP ($8.85), EV/MW ($13.48) and EV/NTM-sales ($17.53), weighted 0.40/0.35/0.20/0.05, gives $6.51. The cash-flow DCF says EV (~$1.33B) is a little below net debt ($1.42B). The SOTP and EV/MW legs credit powered MW at market prices, which is option value.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site FCFF DCF, mid-year from 2026-10-01, split-rate discounting (single-WACC version reported alongside). Each of the 20 inventory sites appears once (see site_coverage). Contracted cash flows at contract terms: Tydal P1-2 $1.003B (single phase from 2027-04-01, yr-1 rent $233M +3%, 90% NOI; in-term cash flow to 2037-04 split 28% LC-backed at 8.5% / 72% Volta-unbacked at 11.0%; 10% Volta default in 2033 and the year-10 stay/walk branch and all re-letting at the 13.9% WACC; $0.5B capex); A102 $0.259B ($160M/yr 2027-31 at 11.5%); A201 $0.218B (70% committed: >$1.7B over 5 yrs = $340M/yr from Q2-27 at 85% probability, discounted at 12%; the uncommitted 30% and the failed-commitment branch at market prices and WACC; 128 racks x $4.0M capex, 50% prepay on committed share); A101 $0.049B (~$30M/yr contracted to end-2028 at 12%, then index decay). At WACC: legacy fleet runoff $0.055B; A202 $0.005B (45% x A102-like GPU cloud at $14M/MW from 2028 = +$0.342B branch; 55% x 10-yr facility fee ~$65M/yr that Bitdeer pays, at 9%, less 50% sublease = -$0.272B branch); refresh cycles $0.183B; mining fleet $0.788B (~80 EH/s on 1,471 energised mining MW); Rockdale HPC 30% x 300 IT MW net of displaced mining $0.130B; mining builds Fox Creek -$0.020B, Massillon +47 MW +$0.018B, Rockdale +179 MW -$0.024B; Tydal P3 $0.028B; Knoxville $0.028B; Wenatchee $0.002B; Clarington $0.065B; Weathersfield $0.068B; Gelephu and Sparks nil; corporate -$1.526B. EV $1.328B less net debt $1.42B = -$0.09B = -$0.34/sh, rolled 12m at Ke 17.3% = -$0.40 (split rate). Same cash flows at a single 13.9% WACC: EV $1.178B, -$1.04/sh. No ATM issuance in the DCF (round-3 supervisor correction); selling ~33M shares at ~$9.50 would lift the figure to ~$0.67, a ~$1.07 transfer from new holders that is not cash-flow value. Sensitivity: life 4y -$2.14, 6y +$0.34, 7y +$0.76; Volta rate 9.5% -$0.15 / 12.5% -$0.62; Rockdale HPC at 60% +$0.16; refresh NPV 0 -$1.49; A202 at 25% -$1.09. 2027E revenue ~$1.74B (mining $1.05B, Tydal $0.175B, AI cloud $0.51B) vs ~$1.56B consensus.

inputs_detail.derivation: Corporate WACC 13.9% unchanged (market weights E $2.90B / D $1.98B). Contracted rate anchor: Bitdeer has no debt priced against any contract yet (inventory contracts_credit); its only secured priced debt is the related-party BIT asset loan at 13.0% effective against rigs and inventory, which is a ceiling, not an anchor. The nearest market anchor is project debt secured on hyperscaler-backstopped AI leases: TeraWulf's WULF Compute 7.75% senior secured notes due 2030 (Fluidstack leases with a $3.2B Google backstop, Oct-2025) and Cipher's Google-backstopped Fluidstack financing. That is ~3.5-4% over Treasuries of the time; on today's 5.29% 10Y that is ~8.5-9%. Tydal's ~$1.3B LCs (~28% of TCV, J.P. Morgan-arranged, still 'anticipated' and conditional) back only part of the rent and the building is not yet delivered, so 8.5% applies to 28% of in-term cash flow. The other 72% rests on Volta (private, unrated, early-stage) and its end customer (reportedly a ~6-yr compute deal, shorter than the lease). I use 11.0%: about single-B yield plus completion risk, below the 13% BIT loan because a signed lease is better collateral than rigs, and below WACC because default is already in the cash flows as a 10% 2033 leg. A102 11.5%: unrated customers, but prepayments cover >50% of capex. A201/A101 12%: unrated, undisclosed, A201 'commitments' not disclosed as executed. A202 fee: Bitdeer's own fixed obligation, so it is discounted at Bitdeer's ~9% pre-tax cost of debt, which makes the cost larger

Bitdeer's own contracts bracket refresh economics: A201 ($11.2M/MW for 5 yrs on $24.5M/MW capex) is ~-7% of capex at 13.9%, A102 ($16.8M/MW) ~+40%. MW-weighted toward A201/A202 scale, ~+10%. A market-priced refresh needs ~$18M/MW year-1 revenue to earn that; today's $12M/MW would lose ~40% of capex, which is why the refresh tail is worth little. Supervisor asked for a justification of +10%. Bitdeer only buys GPUs against prepaid offtakes, so a refresh happens only when it can be contracted. Today's contracts earn +40% (A102) and well above that (A201 at $22.4M/MW), while a market-priced refresh would lose ~40%. +10% assumes most of the current scarcity premium is gone by the 2032+ refresh dates. bear.story: BTC/hashprice falls back to the June lows (~$28/PH/day) or the halving gets priced in early. Mining burns cash, BIT loans ($491M current at 6/30, 13% effective) need collateral top-ups or refinancing, and the $1B ATM is sold below $8. Tydal slips past the 2027-03-31 single-phase delivery or the Volta credit backstop milestone falters. A201 commitments fall through with ~$0.5B of GB300 racks already bought, and A202's 10-yr facility fee runs with no GPUs. Equity is squeezed by ~$2B of gross debt; the price converges on the ~$5-6 DCF value. GPU-cloud pricing normalises faster than contracts can be renewed (H100-style -50% within ~18 months of the next generation), A202 is built without customers, and the market starts valuing the AI cloud on contracted cash flows only.

base.story: Tydal is delivered as one phase around 2027-03-31 and start ~$233M/yr of 90%-margin rent. A102 revenue starts in Q1 2027; A201's >70% commitments (~$340M/yr) convert to revenue from Q2-2027; AI ARR reaches ~$250-350M run-rate by mid-2027. Mining is decent at ~$35-40 hashprice ahead of the 2028 halving. Rockdale HPC talks continue but nothing large is signed. ATM dilution is moderate. The stock trades above the ~$6.6 blended fair value on ARR growth and power optionality; the market does not yet discount the short economic life of GPU-cloud revenue, so the GPU-life rebuild trims the base only modestly.

bull.story: A second large colocation lease (Rockdale 300+ MW, Norway expansion or Ohio) is signed at Tydal-like economics, A201/A202 are fully contracted, and BTC goes back above $110k. The market re-rates BTDR toward the contracted-AI cohort's EV/sales (consensus PT ~$22).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$5.40 the market cap (~$1.47B) is about equal to net debt (~$1.42B, so ~$5.2/sh), and the equity would be worth roughly the Tydal lease alone (~$1.0B at split rates, ~$1.2B at a flat 9%), with nothing for 80 EH/s of mining, the Malaysia AI cloud (A102 + A201 commitments, ~$0.77B in my DCF) or ~2.8 GW of other sites. That is 22% under the 52-week low ($6.92). Getting there would most likely take a Tydal/Volta credit-backstop failure, a refinancing squeeze on the current related-party BIT loans, A201 commitments failing with racks bought, deeply dilutive equity, or a hashprice collapse. Ordinary BTC-beta volatility would not explain it. Unchanged in round 4: the cash-flow DCF (-$0.40) is a floor that sits far below any traded price, so it does not define a break level

Whether Rockdale/Ohio power can be leased to an AI tenant at Tydal-like economics (the main bull driver)
Volta credit backstop milestones and the tenant's no-fee termination right at year 10
Whether A201's >70% 'commitments' are executed and paid (not disclosed as executed), A202 offtake versus its 10-yr facility fee (amount undisclosed); GPU-cloud pricing over 5-yr contracts
Related-party dependence on BIT Group (3,669 BTC loan; $423M asset loan) and controlling-shareholder Class V votes

GPU economic life and post-contract pricing: A102/A201 are 5-yr contracts on GB300-class GPUs; if prices hold up as in 2025-26 (CoreWeave re-contracting near original prices) the AI cloud is worth ~$0.5B (7-yr life), if supply goes long ~$0.1B (4-yr)

Discount rate on Volta's unbacked 72% of Tydal rent: 9.5% to 12.5% moves the DCF from -$0.15 to -$0.62/sh. No Bitdeer debt is priced against the lease yet; the first project financing will set the anchor
reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split-rate discounting). I rebuilt the DCF site by site from the checked inventory (sites.md), so each of its 20 sites appears exactly once, and fixed every flag on my model. (1) A201 (flag 3): re-read the 9/29 release. >70% of 21.7 MW is committed for >$1.7B over 5 yrs ($22.4M/MW-yr, 2x my round-3 price), so I use 85% (commitments are not disclosed as executed), with a market branch, and 128 racks instead of 133 (flag 16). (2) A202 (flag 6): the 10-yr facility fee Bitdeer pays (~$65M/yr, judgment) is charged in every branch, alongside a 45% chance of A102-like GPU cloud. Net ~$0. (3) Rockdale (flag 9): HPC probability cut 60% -> 30% and the displaced mining netted. Value $0.74B -> $0.13B, the biggest single cut. (4) Omitted sites (flags 7, 8, 14) added as probability-weighted builds net of capex. Tydal P3, Knoxville, Wenatchee, Clarington, Weathersfield +$0.19B. Fox Creek, Massillon +47 and Rockdale +179 are ~nil, because post-halving mining builds earn about their cost of capital. Gelephu (LOI) and Sparks are nil. (5) Discounting: Bitdeer has no contract-secured debt, so I anchor on TeraWulf's 7.75% Google-backstopped secured notes, scaled to today's 5.29% 10Y. That gives 8.5% for the ~28% of Tydal rent covered by LCs, 11% for the unbacked Volta share (unrated), 11.5-12% for unrated Malaysia offtakes and 13.9% for everything uncontracted. Tydal falls from $1.185B to $1.003B because round 3 discounted its post-year-10 option and re-letting at 9%. DCF: -$0.40 split-rate, -$1.04 at a single WACC. No ATM transfer (supervisor); ATM issuance at $9.50 would add ~$1.07. SOTP $8.85 and EV/MW $13.48 rise, because Knoxville/Wenatchee and the Malaysia AI cloud are now counted explicitly and A201 is re-priced. With weights shifted toward cash flows (0.40/0.35/0.20/0.05) the blend is $6.51 vs $6.64. A ~2% move, plus roughly offsetting news (A201 confirmed and richer, less Rockdale optionality), does not justify moving the scenarios or ladders. They stay as in round 3: bear $4.8 33% / base $9.0 45% / bull $19.5 22%, P(>=spot) 0.365, median ~$8.6. The 1-month ladder and the $5.40 thesis break are also unchanged. Research this round: 1 WebFetch of the A201 release (primary) and 2 searches for contract-secured financing rates (TeraWulf, Cipher). No options data, nothing under priors/, no other forecasters' files.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contracted MW earn the contract price for the term (A102 $160M/yr 2027-31; A201 committed 70% at $340M/yr for 5 yrs from Q2-2027 (85%); A202 (45%), Knoxville (40%) and Wenatchee (30%) at $14M/MW for 5 yrs). After contract and for uncontracted MW, revenue per MW follows a generation-age index fitted to H100/A100/V100 rents: 1.00 at launch, 0.85 at 1 yr, 0.60 at 2, 0.45 at 3, then ~-12%/yr to 0.30 at 6, 0.22 at 7, 0.13 at 8 (6-yr path; the 5-yr base reaches each level ~20% sooner). That is steep for ~2 yrs after the next generation ships, then flatter. Cohorts run while revenue x (1 - variable opex) exceeds $2.6M/MW-yr of power + DC fees, then are refreshed at $24.5M/MW (+2%/yr) every 5 yrs at hurdle-plus-10% economics.
gpu_life.note: Unchanged approach: contract price for the term, generation-age decay after, cash tail against fixed cost, refresh every 5 yrs at hurdle +10% (4y +2%, 6y +19%, 7y +26%). What changed is coverage and terms. A201 is re-priced to the 9/29 commitments ($22.4M/MW). A101 is carved out as contracted. A202 now carries its facility fee. Knoxville and Wenatchee are added as GPU-cloud pipeline. Malaysia AI cloud is $0.769B (round 3: $0.28B). Split-rate DCF by life: 4y -$2.14, 5y -$0.40, 6y +$0.34, 7y +$0.76 (single WACC: -$2.77 / -$1.04 / -$0.31 / +$0.11). The 5-yr base is kept. The fact-checked company lives (CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 from Jan-2026, IREN 5) bracket it, and Bitdeer itself depreciates GPUs over 4 years and sells 5-yr contracts. Tydal's default leg no longer cites Kerrisdale, which the fact-check could not verify. GPU life still matters less than refresh pricing: refresh NPV 0 moves the DCF -$1.09/sh

discounting.basis: contracted_rate is the blended Tydal in-term rate: 28% of in-term cash flow (the ~$1.3B LC cover / $4.7B TCV) at 8.5% and 72% at 11.0%. A102 is at 11.5%, A201 and A101 at 12.0%, and Bitdeer's own A202 facility fee at 9.0%. Bitdeer has no debt secured on any contract (sites.json contracts_credit). Its only priced secured debt is the related-party BIT loan at 13.0% effective, secured on rigs, which I treat as a ceiling. The 8.5% anchor is TeraWulf's 7.75% senior secured notes against Google-backstopped Fluidstack leases (~3.5-4% over Treasuries then), applied to today's 5.29% 10Y and adjusted for Tydal's completion risk. No counterparty is investment-grade. Volta and the Malaysia GPU customers are unrated, so their rates sit between that anchor and the 13.9% WACC, as justified in the DCF discount-rate row. Post-contract, uncontracted, pipeline, terminal, mining and corporate cash flows are at the 13.9% WACC. Round 3's hybrid (Tydal 9%, rest 13.9%) gives -$0.05 on the round-4 cash flows.
